newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hochtief says restructuring affects result.
newsitem.headline: Hochtief says restructuring affects result.

text.p: The management board chairman of German construction company Hochtief AG said in an interview released on Tuesday that a 10 percent cut in German-based staff this year would have an effect on 1996 profits and dividend.
"Our dividends reflect our results and not a certain (dividend) policy," Hans-Peter Keitel told the financial daily Handelsblatt, according to an advance release from Wednesday's edition.

"But this year the labour factor has claimed a substantial cost to allow us to be equipped for the future. This cannot be completely disregarded in the context of where our result and dividend are going," he said.
At the same time Keitel was optimistic for the future.

"Our order books are pretty full. We have cut our workforce, tightened up our branch network and cut operating costs. On that basis we can record high profits next year even if business volume falls 10 percent."
Last year Hochtief made a net profit of 137 million marks.

Keitel said results had been affected not only by the 20,000 lay-offs in Germany but also by a decline in the share price of Germany's other big construction player Philipp Holzmann AG, in which Hochtief holds a 24.9 percent stake.
Keitel said he still had hopes that Hochtief might eventually succeed in an attempt, blocked by the Federal Cartel Office, to get more influence over Holzmann by raising its stake to 34.9 percent.

He said this would make both firms more competitive internationally in a sector where there was a growing demand for construction firms not only to deliver buildings but also to manage and finance the facilities they had built.
Major French, Japanese and American concerns were currently better at this than the Germans, he said.
"Holzmann and Hochtief have complementary areas of activity abroad, and are an ideal match for each other," Keitel said.

"While we have been active for decades in Australia and Hong Kong, Holzmann long ago got a foothold in Thailand and the United States. Before we set up new branches, it makes much more sense to use our synergies," he said.
He added that there was a "high degree of readiness" at Holzmann to discuss forms of cooperation in a number of areas.
